'''''Crocus tommasinianus''''', the '''woodland crocus''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=CRTO8|taxon=Crocus tommasinianus|accessdate=17 January 2016}}</ref> '''early crocus''',<ref>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> or '''Tommasini's crocus''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family ''[[Iridaceae]]''.<ref name=POWO>{{cite web |url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:436740-1 |title= Crocus tommasinianus Herb. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=30 November 2024}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/ZL48 |title= Crocus tommasinianus Herb. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=30 November 2024}}</ref> It is named after the [[botanist]] [[Muzio Tommasini|Muzio G. Spirito de Tommasini]] (1794–1879). It is [[native plant|native]] to Bulgaria, Hungary, Albania, and the former [[Yugoslavia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=327764 |title=Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families}}</ref> It is often referred to as the early or snow crocus, but these terms are shared with several other species, although ''C. tommasinianus'' is amongst the first to bloom. Multiple plants are often called '''tommies''' in the horticultural trade.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://gardenersapprentice.com/gardeningtips/tommie-crocus/ | title = Tommie Crocus | date = 14 March 2016 | publisher = The Gardener's Apprentice | access-date = 24 January 2022}}</ref>

==Description==

It is a [[corm]]ous [[perennial plant|perennial]] of the [[genus]] ''[[Crocus]]'' in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Iridaceae]] with a lilac flower, and is one of the smaller of the cultivated species. It has slender flowers about {{convert|2|-|4|cm|0|abbr=on}} long, with white perianth tubes, petals (6) pale silvery lilac to reddish purple, while the outer petals may be overlaid with silver and darker tips. A variant, ''C. tommasinianus'' f. ''albus'', is white. Its [[cultivars]] are used as [[ornamental plant]]s. Height: {{convert|3|in|0|abbr=on}}

==Habitat==
The species is found growing around 1000 meters in woods and on shady hillsides, commonly on limestone with flowering occurring in January and February; the narrow leaves are fully developed by the time the purple flowers with white tubes blooms.<ref name="Rix">{{Cite book|last=Phillips|first=Roger|title=The Random House book of bulbs|date=1989|publisher=Random House|others=Martyn Rix, Brian Mathew|isbn=0-679-72756-6|location=New York|oclc=19922564|page=19}}</ref>

==Cultivation==

It naturalizes easily earning an official recognition as a weed and is [[Naturalisation (biology)|naturalized]] in the US state of [[Delaware]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Serviss|first1=Brett E.|last2=Peck|first2=James H.|last3=Benjamin|first3=Kristen R.|title=Crocus Flavus: A New Genus and Species of Non-Native Iridaceae for the Arkansas (U.s.a.) Flora |date=2016|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/44858594|journal=Journal of the Botanical Research Institute of Texas|volume=10|issue=2|pages=513–516|jstor=44858594 |issn=1934-5259}}</ref> It is often planted in large drifts in gardens and parks.

This plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |title=''Crocus tommasinianus'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/25699/Crocus-tommasinianus/Details |website=RHS Gardening |publisher=Royal Horticultural Society |accessdate=2020-04-17}}</ref>
